note: People named in the syllabus (guest lecturers, session leads). Everyone listed here also gets a card in the "Guest lecturers" section of /people, in the order below. A week's track lists `people: ["<id>"]` in syllabus.json and the site renders each id as a chip with a hover card, linking to that person's card at /people#<id>. `id` is the slug used from syllabus.json and is the anchor on the People page, so keep it unique and stable. `name` is shown on the chip, including any title (e.g. "Ms Natasha Banks"). `role` and `affiliation` form the line under the name; either may be an empty string. `bio` is a sentence or two. `achievements` is a short list of bullet points (keep to 2-4; an empty list hides the section). `photo` is optional and falls back to initials: put the image in public/people/, named after the id (e.g. public/people/natasha-banks.jpeg), and reference it as "/people/<id>.<ext>". A square headshot of about 400px is plenty; it is only ever shown as an avatar. `href` is optional and points somewhere else on the web that is theirs (LinkedIn, their own site, their employer's staff page); their card on /people shows it as a "More about" link and hides it when absent. It is not their profile on this site: the syllabus chip and the hover card always link to /people#<id>.

people.name: Natasha Banks
people.bio: Natasha (Tash) Banks is the Program Director for Day of AI Australia, a free world-class AI literacy program for teachers and students K-12 across Australia. Her mission is to empower young Australians to understand AI, act as responsible and safe users, and confidently shape the AI-powered world of the future. Tash brings over a decade of experience in project management, operations, and stakeholder engagement. She previously served as Head of Operations at Future Women and has held roles at the Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC).
